label: Vossmark Grunt -- Polish Pass (v2)
note: Baseline trooper, light polish only: the mouth was a 7px-wide solid white block reading as a cartoon grin, narrowed to a 3px closed stern line. Silhouette otherwise kept as the Vossmark family baseline that Quota Enforcer and Riot Enforcer differentiate from.

label: Quota Enforcer -- Distinct Silhouette (v1)
note: Was sharing the Grunt's full soldier shape. Redesigned as a corporate labor-enforcer, not a soldier: bare head (no helmet), visible unshadowed face, a lighter vest instead of plate armor, narrower silhouette overall -- still carries the established baton. Self-caught and fixed a missing-arm bug before presenting: the raised baton-hand had a 5-row gap with nothing connecting it to the shoulder (same category of bug as Merc's original missing arm).

label: Riot Enforcer -- Distinct Silhouette (v1)
note: Was sharing the Grunt's shape. Redesigned as the bulkiest of the three: full face-shield helmet (no visible face at all), a riot shield on one arm, baton on the other, wider shoulders, shin guards. Self-caught a subtler bug: the shield and baton each had their own full outline touching the torso's outline, and two adjacent near-black outline pixels read as a background gap at this scale even with no actual transparent dot between them -- merged them into shared single boundaries instead.

label: Splice Husk -- Bespoke Silhouette (v2)
note: Was 100% blob (zero sprite work ever done). Design doc lock: 'unsettling, not graphic' -- wrongness via shape/asymmetry and color, not gore. Anchored to this game's own Phthora ('hollow-eyed... bioluminescent rupture') and Proteus ('peeled chest around a glowing core') bosses so the Specimen Wing reads as smaller-scale echoes of the same origin-point transformation; reused Phthora's exact bioluminescent green (#7ae0a0) as the family's throughline glow, barely visible yet at this tier (a single pinprick). Gaunt hollow-eyed head, one arm visibly withered/shorter than the other, a broken restraint cuff fused to the other wrist, torn clinical smock, uneven dragging stance. v1 self-QA found the two-eye asymmetry fused into one flat dark bar (the 'gecko-eye' spacing mistake again) and the arm/cuff detail was only 1px wide and didn't read as limbs -- v2 narrows the torso by a column each side to give the arms real width and rebuilds the eyes with an actual skin gap between them.

label: Bio-Tank -- Bespoke Silhouette (v1)
note: Was 100% blob. 'A restrained containment specimen that breaks loose' -- bulkier than Husk with ASYMMETRIC swelling on one side (the overgrowth read carries the Regen mechanic visually), a broken harness strap still crossing the chest with a snapped buckle, and a bigger bioluminescent-green rupture on the swollen side than Husk's single pinprick -- same Phthora-green family, escalating with tier. Wider braced stance for the 'tank' read.

label: Chimera Specimen -- Bespoke 24x32 (v1)
note: Was 100% blob. Design doc explicitly locks this one as fully bespoke, NOT a hive-shape reuse -- kept human-adjacent-wrong (a swollen bone-spur claw mass) rather than insectoid, so the Erebus connection stays in flavor text only, per the doc's own constraint. Restraint straps have fused INTO the torso (wrapped bands the skin has grown over -- unnatural fusion, not gore), one arm still ends in a human hand with a torn cuff (the 'these were people' tragic note even at elite tier), the other is a fused overgrown claw-limb, a large asymmetric bioluminescent rupture across the chest (the biggest of the family, echoing Phthora's chest rupture at a smaller scale), and one leg ends in a root-like stump instead of a foot (echoing Phthora's root-tendril motif in miniature). Reads noticeably better than Husk/Tank at this larger canvas -- consistent with the session's established lesson that 16x16 caps how much detail actually lands.

label: [STASHED] Cyborg Gunner — bionic-arm mob idea
note: Not an active candidate -- salvaged from a rejected Merc rifle-arm redesign that read as a bionic/prosthetic arm rather than a held rifle (gunmetal fused directly into the shoulder/arm as one continuous limb). That failure mode is exactly the right READ for a cyborg mob. Revisit when doing mob work; needs a new palette/nature (synthetic augmented-human) and probably a new mob-scale shape, not literally this hero-scale grid.
